label: Founded modern semantics with distinction between Sense and Reference
description: Gottlob Frege formulated and introduced the concept of "Sense and Reference (Sinn und Bedeutung)", which became a seminal contribution in logic philosophy.
dialecticalTension: Formulating an epistemic apparatus to resolve central problems in logic.
historicalContext: Introduced during the 19th Century Divergences as part of Gottlob Frege's canonical writings.

label: Frege's predicate logic and logicism formed the bedrock of Principia Mathematica
description: Bertrand Russell was fundamentally influenced by Gottlob Frege's central inquiries, which shaped the evolution of their philosophical worldview.
dialecticalTension: Negotiating the intellectual shift from Gottlob Frege's perspective to Bertrand Russell's reconstructed system.
historicalContext: Inter-epochal reception: transmitting insights from the 19th Century Divergences across history into the 20th Century Phenomenon & Analysis.

label: Primary intellectual mentor alongside Russell for Wittgenstein's Tractatus
description: Frege's modern quantificational logic and distinction between Sense and Reference (Sinn und Bedeutung) formed the bedrock for Wittgenstein's Tractatus Logico-Philosophicus, which delineated the logical bounds of what can be meaningfully said.
dialecticalTension: Frege's objective third realm of logical thoughts versus Wittgenstein's picture theory of language and the boundary of saying and showing.
historicalContext: Jena and Cambridge, 1911–1919. Wittgenstein visited Frege in Jena, who directed him to study with Bertrand Russell at Cambridge.

citations.author: Ludwig Wittgenstein
citations.quote: I am indebted to Frege's great works and to the writings of my friend Mr Bertrand Russell for much of the stimulation of my thoughts... Whereof one cannot speak, thereof one must be silent.
